papers.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
papers.abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. A novelty of our method is building a connection between the $s$-principal submatrix problem and low-rank singular value perturbations. We also provide an algorithm to determine a positive definite matrix that realizes the given global and local symplectic spectra. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.

papers.title: Displaceability of monotone Lagrangians in $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$
papers.abstract: We show that the generalized Polterovich submanifold $L_{0, 2}^P$ in $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and the Chekanov-Oakley-Usher Lagrangian $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ in the quadric $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$ are displaceable. Since $L_{0, 2}^P$ and $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ are in the zero level set of the moment maps of the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-actions on $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$, the main idea is to construct Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms mapping $L_{0, 2}^P$ and $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ to nonzero level sets of the moment maps.

papers.title: On Gutt-Hutchings capacities of Minkowski sums and products of convex domains
papers.abstract: For Minkowski p-sums of convex domains, we establish Brunn-Minkowski-type inequalities for the full sequence of Gutt-Hutchings capacities. We also obtain explicitlower bounds for the Gutt-Hutchings capacities of Minkowski p-products. Our proof uses Matijevic's formula for Gutt-Hutchings capacities in terms of the Clarke dual-action functional and the Fadell-Rabinowitz index. By the equality of Gutt-Hutchings and Ekeland-Hofer capacities on star-shaped domains, the same inequalities hold for Ekeland-Hofer capacities.

papers.title: Exploration of vertical self-resonant bifurcations from Distant Retrograde Orbits (DROs) in the Earth-Moon Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP)
papers.abstract: This paper investigates vertical self-resonant bifurcations from the Distant Retrograde Orbit (DRO) family in the Earth-Moon circular restricted three-body problem. Using a predictor-corrector continuation algorithm, we identify fourteen vertical-critical DROs consisting of twelve higher-order periods of multiplicity from integer multiples of five to ten and two vertical pitchfork bifurcations. Their continuation generates twenty-five families of spatial symmetric periodic orbits. Beyond the computation of new periodic orbit families, the main contribution of this work is a systematic characterization of the resulting global bifurcation topology through symplectic invariants. To this end, we combine Floquet multiplier transitions at local bifurcations with Conley-Zehnder indices, Krein signatures and the Euler characteristic of the local Floer homology to develop a computational symplectic framework that systematically classifies the bifurcated families and provides a topological interpretation of their numerically established connections. The computations reveal a global bifurcation network generated by the DRO family, including bridge families that connect the DROs with Butterfly, planar prograde and P3DRO families, together with several families consisting of long-period multi-excursion orbits that approach collision with the Moon. The computations also identify spatial periodic orbits satisfying Earth-Moon resonances along several bifurcated families.

papers.title: Biran decomposition and relative symplectic cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed monotone integral symplectic manifold with monotonicity constant $\tau>0$, and let $D\subset M$ be a symplectic hyperplane section of degree $0<k<\tau$. By Biran's decomposition theorem, $M$ is the union of a symplectic disk bundle over $D$ and the skeleton of the complement $M\setminus D$ equipped with its Liouville structure. In this paper, we compute the relative symplectic cohomology of circle subbundles of this disk bundle over $\mathbb{Z}$ in terms of the quantum cohomology of $D$. This relative symplectic cohomology depends on the radius of the circle bundle relative to a certain critical radius. For a broad class of pairs $(M,D)$, we prove that the relative symplectic cohomology over $\mathbb{Z}$ does not vanish for supercritical radii. Therefore, circle bundles of supercritical radii are heavy subsets, which yields infinite dimensional quasi-flats in the Hamiltonian diffeomorphism group with respect to both the Hofer metric and the spectral metric over $\mathbb{Z}$. We also establish that if the degree $k$ of $D$ is greater than one, the skeleton of $M\setminus D$ is SH-full over $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$, and hence non-displaceable in $M$ by any symplectomorphism.
